speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for seeing me. You mentioned a worsening headache and vision changes over three weeks; can you describe the exact nature of the headache, such as its location and severity?

speaker: Patient
text: 69-year-old woman. The patient reports a 3-week history of headache and progressively worsening vision. She has not noticed any other symptoms, including no recent weight changes, no fevers, no night sweats, and no pain elsewhere in the body.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Since you are a 69-year-old with progressive vision loss and headaches, have you noticed any specific visual deficits, such as a curtain coming over your vision, halos around lights, or double vision?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Headache. I also have Worsening vision over the past 3 weeks, No weight changes, No fevers, No night sweats, No other pain. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Tuberculosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Tuberculous Meningitis.

The patient's history of chronic headache, progressive vision changes, and the physician's specific identification of a "typical" TB presentation strongly point to this diagnosis, especially given the exclusion of fever and night sweats which can occur in chronic cases. I will proceed with ordering a lumbar puncture to confirm the diagnosis.
